subquestions.subquestion: Highest daily hops for one aircraft on one flight number
subquestions.answer_markdown: The longest single-day itineraries are dominated by Southwest Airlines (WN), which operates a point-to-point network where a single aircraft can fly the same flight number through many legs in one day. The record is a 9-hop American Airlines flight 1086 on 1988-11-12 (tail number unknown in early data) routing TPA-BNA-OMA-DSM-BNA-RSW-SRQ-DFW-DFW-OKC. All remaining top-10 unique routes have 8 hops and are operated by Southwest between 2021 and 2024. Route recurrence ranges from 1 day (one-time occurrence) to 46 days across history, with the most frequent being WN flight 2884 routing LGA-STL-ICT-DEN-COS-PHX-ELP-HOU-JAN (46 days) and WN flight 1956 routing MSY-TPA-BWI-ORD-DEN-SLC-LAS-BUR-SJC (40 days).
subquestions.sql:
WITH legs AS (
    SELECT
        Tail_Number,
        Flight_Number_Reporting_Airline,
        IATA_CODE_Reporting_Airline AS Carrier,
        FlightDate,
        count() AS hop_count,
        arrayStringConcat(
            arrayMap(x -> x.2, arraySort(x -> x.1,
                groupArray((assumeNotNull(CRSDepTime), OriginCode)))),
            '-'
        ) || '-' || arrayElement(
            arrayMap(x -> x.2, arraySort(x -> x.1,
                groupArray((assumeNotNull(CRSDepTime), DestCode)))),
            -1
        ) AS Route
    FROM ontime.fact_ontime
    WHERE Cancelled = 0 AND CRSDepTime IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY Tail_Number, Flight_Number_Reporting_Airline, IATA_CODE_Reporting_Airline, FlightDate
),
route_stats AS (
    SELECT Route, uniqExact(FlightDate) AS recurrence_count
    FROM legs
    GROUP BY Route
),
recent_per_route AS (
    SELECT
        l.Tail_Number,
        l.Flight_Number_Reporting_Airline,
        l.Carrier,
        l.FlightDate,
        l.hop_count,
        l.Route,
        rs.recurrence_count,
        row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY l.Route ORDER BY l.FlightDate DESC) AS rn
    FROM legs l
    JOIN route_stats rs ON l.Route = rs.Route
)
SELECT
    Tail_Number,
    Flight_Number_Reporting_Airline,
    Carrier,
    FlightDate,
    hop_count,
    Route,
    recurrence_count
FROM recent_per_route
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY hop_count DESC, FlightDate DESC
LIMIT 10

subquestions.subquestion: Do the top itineraries appear to be recurring scheduled patterns or mostly one-offs?
subquestions.answer_markdown: The top 10 itineraries show a mixed picture but lean toward recurrence: only 2 routes are true one-offs (recurrence_count = 1), while 8 of 10 appeared on multiple days. Three routes appeared 2–5 days (rare), three appeared 6–20 days (semi-regular), and two appeared on 40 and 46 distinct days respectively, indicating genuine scheduled patterns. The two highly recurring routes — WN 1956 (MSY-TPA-BWI-ORD-DEN-SLC-LAS-BUR-SJC, 40 days) and WN 2884 (LGA-STL-ICT-DEN-COS-PHX-ELP-HOU-JAN, 46 days) — are clearly scheduled Southwest rotations flown repeatedly across multiple years. Overall, the majority of top 8-hop itineraries are not accidental or irregular; they reflect a repeating scheduling pattern.

WITH legs AS (
    SELECT
        FlightDate,
        count() AS hop_count,
        arrayStringConcat(
            arrayMap(x -> x.2, arraySort(x -> x.1,
                groupArray((assumeNotNull(CRSDepTime), OriginCode)))),
            '-'
        ) || '-' || arrayElement(
            arrayMap(x -> x.2, arraySort(x -> x.1,
                groupArray((assumeNotNull(CRSDepTime), DestCode)))),
            -1
        ) AS Route
    FROM ontime.fact_ontime
    WHERE Cancelled = 0 AND CRSDepTime IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY Tail_Number, Flight_Number_Reporting_Airline, IATA_CODE_Reporting_Airline, FlightDate
),
route_stats AS (
    SELECT Route, uniqExact(FlightDate) AS recurrence_count
    FROM legs
    GROUP BY Route
),
recent_per_route AS (
    SELECT
        l.FlightDate,
        l.hop_count,
        l.Route,
        rs.recurrence_count,
        row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY l.Route ORDER BY l.FlightDate DESC) AS rn
    FROM legs l
    JOIN route_stats rs ON l.Route = rs.Route
),
top10 AS (
    SELECT Route, hop_count, recurrence_count, FlightDate
    FROM recent_per_route
    WHERE rn = 1
    ORDER BY hop_count DESC, FlightDate DESC
    LIMIT 10
)
SELECT
    multiIf(recurrence_count = 1, 'one-off (1 day)',
            recurrence_count <= 5, 'rare (2-5 days)',
            recurrence_count <= 20, 'semi-regular (6-20 days)',
            'frequent (21+ days)') AS frequency_class,
    count() AS n_routes,
    min(recurrence_count) AS min_days,
    max(recurrence_count) AS max_days
FROM top10
GROUP BY frequency_class
ORDER BY min_days

subquestions.subquestion: What geographic pattern do the top itineraries show?
subquestions.answer_markdown: The top itineraries are overwhelmingly domestic US and transcontinental in scope, reflecting Southwest Airlines' hub-free point-to-point model. Nine of the ten routes are WN flights; most span 7–9 states and touch both the East and West coasts in a single day. Typical routes connect Southern or Midwestern origin cities (MSY, HOU, BWI, LGA) to California terminals (OAK, BUR, SJC, LAX) via a chain of intermediate stops. The sole regionally concentrated route — SMF-SAN-PHX-COS-DEN-PSP-OAK-RNO-LAS — stays within just 4 western states (AZ, CA, CO, NV). There is no single geographic corridor; rather, these are zigzag cross-country circuits that exploit Southwest's flexible scheduling to maximize aircraft utilization across the full continental US.

            '-'

                groupArray((assumeNotNull(CRSDepTime), DestCode)))),
            -1

    FROM ontime.fact_ontime
    WHERE Cancelled = 0 AND CRSDepTime IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY Tail_Number, Flight_Number_Reporting_Airline, IATA_CODE_Reporting_Airline, FlightDate
),
route_stats AS (
    SELECT Route, uniqExact(FlightDate) AS recurrence_count
    FROM legs
    GROUP BY Route
),
recent_per_route AS (
    SELECT
        l.FlightDate,
        l.hop_count,
        l.Route,
        rs.recurrence_count,
        row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY l.Route ORDER BY l.FlightDate DESC) AS rn
    FROM legs l
    JOIN route_stats rs ON l.Route = rs.Route
),
top10 AS (
    SELECT Route, hop_count
    FROM recent_per_route
    WHERE rn = 1
    ORDER BY hop_count DESC, FlightDate DESC
    LIMIT 10
),
route_airports AS (
    SELECT
        t.Route,
        t.hop_count,
        arrayJoin(splitByChar('-', t.Route)) AS airport_code
    FROM top10 t
)
SELECT
    ra.Route,
    ra.hop_count,
    groupUniqArray(d.StateCode) AS states_covered,
    uniq(d.StateCode) AS n_states
FROM route_airports ra
JOIN ontime.dim_airports d ON ra.airport_code = d.AirportCode AND d.IsLatest = 1
GROUP BY ra.Route, ra.hop_count
ORDER BY ra.hop_count DESC, n_states DESC
